name: section4c_spatula_slip
purpose: Gripper-spatula manipulation task for the paper's section 4.3.

what: Two ellipsoidal finger pads squeeze a cylindrical spatula handle while a
square wave modulates the grip. The spatula slides through the fingers
for the whole run in every representation: the baseline grip is
deliberately marginal, which is what makes this a slip test rather than
scene.contact: ellipsoid on cylinder, so the equal-pressure surface is curved
why_this_scene: It is the only frictional, tangential, stick-slip contact in the study.
Section 4.1 found affine voxels fragmenting on curved contact and
section 4.2 found no fragmentation at all on the flat disk face, so
fragmentation was left as a property of curved surfaces with no evidence
that it costs anything. The paper's own open-questions list says a
fragmented patch is most likely to cause trouble in tangential contact
and that nothing tested it. This scene is that test.

why: The earlier ten-run tier study measured trajectory error and cost only.
It could see that affine voxels behaved worst and could not say why, and
it recorded a 47.7 m position RMS for the coarse affine run as though
fragmentation: num_components and largest_component_area_fraction per finger, from the
CalcComponentStats already shared with the settling and disk studies.
Measured: affine voxels reach 67 components per finger with the largest
holding 2.7 percent of the area; tetrahedra and marching cubes give
exactly one component. This is what links affine's grip to the defect
sap_effort: Per-sample iteration and line-search counts. Both other studies found
the count pinned at one, so the solver axis had no range anywhere in the
paper. Here it does: 2.2 mean and 8 to 9 maximum iterations, with up to
38 line-search iterations. Whether it separates the representations is
the result rather than a precondition -- on the smoke run the three
task_outcome: held, first_contact_loss_time_s and handle_axis_slip_m. A dropped run's
position diverges as free fall, so an RMS against a reference measures
the length of the fall. The analysis now reports no trajectory error for
a dropped run and reports when it was dropped instead.
Slip is projected onto the initial handle direction and accumulated only
while held, so it stays about sliding through the fingers rather than
about the spatula's own rotation. Caveat: the spatula rotates by up to
0.86 rad in some runs, and projecting on the initial axis understates
sliding once it has. Swing is reported separately rather than folded in.

refinement.what: Resolution at the baseline grip. Trajectory accuracy and cost.
why_serial: These wall times are the paper's cost data for this section, and this
workload degrades under contention, so a shared machine would make
why_no_fourth_tier: A three-way tier at 0.125 would sit on the reference itself. The
frozen-scene second-order forecast leaves only 1.2x margin over the
measured 10x reference-floor limit there, and at 0.0625 the forecast
is below the limit. The stub text in the paper says four tiers; that
is stale, not a missing run.

grip.what: Grip force at each resolution. The threshold that holds the object.
why: Trajectory RMS compares representations on a task all of them passed.
The coarse affine run does not pass it: the gripper drops the spatula
at 23.3 s. A ratio of position errors cannot express that, and a
threshold force can -- how much more grip a representation needs to
hold what another holds is one number and a physical one.
A smoke sweep at 1.0 and 1.5 N found tetrahedra and marching cubes
holding at both and affine failing at both, so affine's threshold is
above the baseline and the range has to reach well past it. The upper
end is 6 N because the square wave adds 5 N on top of the baseline.
why_concurrent: This sweep reports pass or fail, so contention cannot corrupt the
result. Wall times are still recorded and flagged timing_valid=false.
Each run holds about 50 MiB, so concurrency is bounded by cores rather
than memory -- the opposite of the disk study.
expected_wall_time_note: Bounded by the seven marching-cubes runs at the finer tier, 1706 s
each, which all fit in the 16 slots at once. Serial the sweep would

dropped_run.rule: A run whose final sample has no spatula contact reports no trajectory error
why: Free fall dominates every trajectory channel afterwards. The coarse
affine run read 47.7 m position RMS and 223 m maximum, which is the
distance fallen from t = 23.3 s, not an accuracy. Outcome fields stay
populated because 'dropped at 23.3 s' is the finding.

fragmentation_fraction.rule: Only samples with a patch contribute to the minimum area fraction
why: A no-contact sample leaves the field at zero, and a minimum over those
would report total fragmentation for a gripper that simply let go.

outputs: runs.csv and timing/*.json -- cost, serial only
trajectories/*.csv -- per-sample, now with components and SAP effort
trajectory_metrics.csv -- accuracy and outcome per tier case
supersedes: The ten-run tier study of 2026-08-17, which predates the fragmentation
and SAP columns and recorded the dropped run's free fall as an error.
